heading.en: Backward ukemi (uke takes the breakfall while falling backwards)

prose.en: In order to acquire the throwing techniques, it is first important to acquire ukemi thoroughly, so that the body can be handled safely. When a person is actually thrown, the cases divide broadly into two: the case where uke takes the breakfall while falling forwards (Photo ①), and the case where uke takes the breakfall while falling backwards (Photo ②). When tori applies the technique correctly and holds uke firmly (red mark), and uke takes the breakfall himself or herself, the throw can be made safely without striking the head. In teaching, it is important, from the introductory stage onwards, to work on the idea that the two students acquire the technique through cooperation: throwing and being thrown in pairs: while learning the relationship between tori and uke. For that purpose, step-by-step practice of ukemi that emphasises its connection with the throwing techniques, as shown below, is particularly important.

heading.en: ① From a face-up lying position

prose.en: Point: Crossing the hands makes it easier to strike the tatami. (The red circle marks the crossed hands.) From a face-up lying position, tuck in the chin, raise the head, and bring both arms up in front of the chest. With the palms facing downwards, strike the tatami simultaneously with the whole of both arms. Open both arms 30 to 40 degrees from the sides of the body. If you press the arms down onto the tatami, a strong shock remains, so make them bounce off instantly.

heading.en: ② From a long sitting position

prose.en: Point: By stretching both legs up towards the ceiling, you stop the rotation. From a posture with both legs and both arms stretched out to the front, round the back and lower the upper body backwards; fall as though rolling while stretching both legs out, and at the instant the back of the belt touches the tatami, strike the tatami strongly with both arms. So as not to strike the back of the head, tuck in the chin and keep looking at the knot of the belt until the very end.

Point: When you are actually thrown backwards, you will be taking the breakfall with one arm. Once students get used to it, have them practise the one-armed rear breakfall alternately on the left and right.

heading.en: Faults that are easy to fall into

prose.en: The ushiro-ukemi that is practised first is the foundation of all breakfalls. At this stage it is important to have students master the three important elements of ukemi and to acquire a firm foundation in ukemi.

First, students acquire the feel of striking the tatami. Make them conscious that they strike the tatami with the whole forearm and palm, that the pain is only momentary, and that by doing this they protect important parts of the body such as the head and the internal organs. This is sometimes called *mae-ukemi* (the forward breakfall).
At first use a helper; then gradually let students control the roll on their own so that they do not strike their heads.
At the instant of striking the tatami, the neck muscles are tensed. It is especially effective for girls, whose neck muscles are weaker, to begin with this practice.
Once students are used to it, the helper places a hand on the partner's forehead and checks how firmly the neck is tensed.

From the half-crouch posture with both arms stretched forward, lower the buttocks close to the heels, fall backward and take the ukemi (breakfall). In the second half, stop the rotation by directing and extending both legs upward.
From the standing posture, bend both knees while lowering the buttocks close to the heels, fall backward and take the ukemi.

heading.en: ア Ushiro-ukemi (rear breakfall) while moving forward

prose.en: Walk two or three steps forward, then take the ushiro-ukemi.
Walk two or three steps backward, then take the ushiro-ukemi.

When, because of changes in lifestyle, there are students who are poor at crouching, work in pairs: raising the starting posture in stages, slowly lower the buttocks close to the heels and take the breakfall backward.
Once students are used to taking ukemi, the helper checks whether they can still take the breakfall securely even when momentum is added.

Imagining the situation of unintentionally slipping on ice, swing one leg up and, using the other foot as a support, take the breakfall to the rear. This is the way of taking ukemi when techniques that throw you backward, such as ō-soto-gari (major outer reap) or ko-uchi-gari (minor inner reap), are applied. The technique of taking ukemi while falling backward is the key to safety instruction in protecting the back of the head. Not only in judo lessons but also from the standpoint of preventing accidents in everyday life, it is important to incorporate it into warm-up exercises and to build proficiency through repetition.

第４章　技能指導の要点
⑷　受け身
　○前の受け身（受が前に倒れながら受け身を取る）
　○後ろの受け身（受が後ろに倒れながら受け身を取る）
　投げ技を身に付けるためには、まず安全に身をこなすための受け身をしっかりと身に付け
ること大切です。実際に投げられた場合、受が前に倒れながら受け身をとる場合写真①と後
ろへ倒れながら受け身をとる場合写真②の二つに大別されます。取が正しく技をかけ、受を
しっかりと保持（赤印）し、受が自ら受け身を取るようにすることで、頭部を打つことなく
安全に投げることができます。指導にあたっては、初歩の段階から、２人１組で投げる、投
げられるなど取と受の関係性を学びながら2人の協力で技を身に付けるという発想が大切です。
そのためには、以下に示すような投げ技との関連を重視した受け身の段階的な練習が特に重
要となります。
取が「膝車」をかけ、受が「横受け身」をとる。
取が「大腰」をかけ、受が「前回り受け身」をとる。
後ろの受け身のイメージ
写真②
取が「大外刈り」をかけ、受が「後ろ受け身」をとる

第４章　技能指導の要点
　③　中腰の姿勢から
　中腰で両腕を前に伸ばした姿勢から、臀部を踵の近くに下ろし、後ろに倒れて受け身をとります。
後半、両脚を上方に向け伸ばすことで回転を止めます。
　④　立位の姿勢から
　立位の姿勢から両膝を曲げながら臀部を踵の近くに下ろし、後ろに倒れて受け身をとります。
　⑤　移動しながら
　　ア　前に移動しながらの後ろ受け身
　２～３歩前に歩いて、後ろ受け身をとります。
　　イ　後ろに移動しながらの後ろ受け身
　２～３歩後ろに歩いて、後ろ受け身をとります。
